added_lines: praying for the dead in november we remember and pray for the dead. the november dead lists are in the church here at holy cross so that you may inscribe the names of your loved ones. their names will be included in the prayers of our daily mass during this month. we remember them fondly but also pray for them because we recognise that every person who has died is in need of god’s mercy. it is a relationship of love that we have with them; we love them on earth and therefore wish for them to now enter heaven to enjoy god’s mercy. the concept of time beyond the grave is difficult to comprehend. however, the catholic practice of praying for the dead is to ask for god’s mercy in their lives, to purify them so that they may see god face to face. we can think of praying for the dead in terms of the relationship that god has had with a person in life, which continues in death. our prayers and the celebration of the mass can help them to know god’s mercy and be carried up into the embrace of god. the prayer ‘eternal rest grant unto them o lord, and let perpetual light shine upon them, may they rest in peace, amen’ summarises our prayer. it is an invitation to the gift of god’s mercy so that the person may know peace and joy in the company of the saints in heaven. the church has always urged us to pray for the dead. she invites believers to regard the mystery of death not as the final word on human fate but as a journey towards eternal life. it is an important duty of ours to pray for the dead because, although they may have died in grace and in friendship with god, they may still be in need of a final purification in order to enter into the joy of heaven. we are all one body in christ; we are part of the communion of saints - a belief which we express whenever we recite the apostles creed. because of their closeness to god, the saints in heaven can intercede with him for both the living and the dead, especially those who have died and are still in purgatory. st john vianney said, “we can assist the dead through our prayers, our good works and, above all, the holy sacrifice of the mass. ” as the scriptures state, “whatever you did for one of these least brothers of mine, you did for me ” (matthew 25:40). purgatory is not a place but a process of purification for souls who die in god’s grace but are not yet perfectly holy. pope benedict xvi stated, “ purgatory essentially means that god can put the pieces back together again. that he can cleanse us in such a way that we are able to be with him and can stand there in the fullness of life. purgatory strips off from one person what is unbearable and from another the inability to bear certain things, so that in each of them a pure heart is revealed, and we can see that we all belong together in one enormous symphony of being. ” it is important to remember however the mercy of god. one of the most repeated sentences in the scriptures is the words: mercy of god endures forever. it is said twenty-six times in psalm 136 and can also be found in jeremiah 33:11 “give thanks to yahweh sabaoth, for yahweh is good, for his mercy is everlasting ”. the word for mercy, “chesedh”, is used one hundred and fifty times in the old testament. for example from numbers 14:19 we find moses praying: “in the abundance of your mercy forgive the sins of your people”. father charles the mass for all those who celebrated a funeral in holy cross from oct 2025-october 2026 will take place on monday 2nd november, feast of all souls at 7pm. eternal rest, grant to them olord and let perpetual light website : www .ballymoneyparish.com facebook : @ballymoneycatholic youtube : ballymoney parish november the month of the holy souls next week we begin the month of special prayer for the holy souls. there are a number of ways that we can pray together as a parish for our deceased loved ones this year. november dead lists and envelopes are now available. please take them home and write down the names of your deceased family and friends who you wish to pray for. envelopes can be left back in the church at mass times or posted through the door of the parochial house. the names will be placed before the altar throughout the month of november and prayed for at all masses and devotions. you may wish to include an offering in your envelope and these are very gratefully received. prayer & reßection there will be two short services of prayer and reßection on the theme of remembering the dead and the resurrection during the month. the þrst will be on thursday 5th november at 7pm . parish annual requiem mass a requiem mass for all deceased parishioners and priests will take place on friday 13th november at 7pm . november pledge why not go off alcohol (or another treat) this month as a penance for the holy souls? think of it as a little lent in november (and a good preparation for christmas too!). if you wish to make the pledge you can pray: i promise, in honour of the sacred heart of jesus, and with the help of the blessed virgin mary, to abstain from all intoxicating substances until the end of november. please consider joining with others in prayer, sacriþce and support for those affected by addiction. hymns for mass make me a channel of your peace. where there is hatred let me bring your love. where there is injury, your pardon, lord and where there's doubt, true faith in you. make me a channel of your peace where there's despair in life, let me bring hope where there is darkness, only light and where there's sadness, ever joy. o, master grant that i may never seek so much to be consoled as to console to be understood as to understand to be loved as to love with all my soul. make me a channel of your peace it is in pardoning that we are pardoned in giving to all men that we receive and in dying that we're born to eternal life. now thank we all our god with heart and hands and voices, who wondrous things has done, in whom his world rejoices; who from our mothers' arms has blessed us on our way with countless gifts of love, and still is ours today. omay this bounteous god through all our life be near us, with ever joyful hearts and blessed peace to cheer us, to keep us in his grace, and guide us when perplexed, and free us from all ills of this world in the next. ballymoney

a lot of people do not like large gatherings. they find bigcrowds exhausting. today’s feast, however, is precisely about crowds of people. the first reading expresses it well, ‘ a huge number, impossible to count… , today is the feast not just of a few chosen saints, but of all saints. today we honour all the saints, those who are formally canonised and those who ar not. if our vision of humanity is shaped exclusively by the media we might be tempted to think that there are a lot more villains out there than saints. it is reassuring to be reminded by today’s feast that there exists a huge number of saints, impos sible to count. in the words of the letter to the hebrews, we are surrounded by a ‘ great cloud of witnesses’ . none of us can live as the lord wants us to live purely on our own. we need the good example of others to inspire us and to what is possible. today’s feast declares that we are surrounded by such a cloud of witnesses , if only we could recognise them. some of these people have already passed beyond us and are now ‘ standing in front of the throne of the lamb’ , in the words of today’s first reading. many of them, however, are our companions on the journey of life. they do not look at all like the statues in our churches. they are very ordinary, yet they are also very special. these are the people we are grateful to h avemet and to have around. the feast of all saints encourages us to believe that any one of us could be part o f that huge number, impossible to count. in that sense, today’s feast is about every one of us. john, in today’s second reading, is speaking about all of us when he declares that ‘ we are already the children of god’, and that, in the future, ‘ we shall be like’ god. we are all destined for sainthood. god intends that all of us would be conformed to the image of god’s son. for most of us, that will only come to pass fully beyond this life. yet, because we are already sons and daughters of god through baptism, we are called to grow now towards that wonderful transformation that awaits us. the road to sainthood begins here, wherever we happen to find o urselves. in today’s gospel reading, jesus shows us what that road to sainthood looks like. in the beatitudes, jesus painted a portrait of himself, the livings aint par excellence. he was also painting a portrait of the person that we are all call ed to become. the beatitudes give us different facets of the person of jesus, while at the same time showing us different ways in which we might reflect the person o f jesu feast of all saints 1st november 2026 very rev. canon colm mcbride pp : parochial house 44 lough road loughguile bt44 9jn tel:

veronica arthurs(1st,) vincent o’rourke, mildred donnelly, charles kelly, eddie west(snr,) michael nicholson, michael dorrian, frank cafolla, dominic hughes francesca phillips, elizabeth magliocco, john faloona, eileen & eugene mcgarrity. indulgences for the holy souls during the month of november the church urges us to pray ferve ntly for the holy souls in purgatory. the motivation behind our praye r is to free the deceased of the effects of their sins so that the lord will welcome them to the happiness of heaven. through our prayer, we can also gain plenary indulgences for the holy souls, that is the remission of temporal punishment due to sin, for sins already forgiven. 1st-8th november-by those who visit a cemetery, praying for the holy souls and praying for the intentions of the holy father, including the our father and the apostle’s creed. 2nd november- feast of all souls-by those who make a visit to the blessed sacrament in the church and there pray for the holy souls including prayer for the holy father’s intentions, including the our father and the apostle’s creed. in order to obtain the plenary indulgence for the holy souls, we need to be in the state of grace, that is, we must have attended the sacrament of confession, and received holy communion recently. supporting the work of the church this weekend are two collections, the weekly offering in support of the parish and the monthly offering in support of the priests of the diocese. thanks to those who contributed so generously to the collections of last weekend. the weekly offering came to £1308. donations to the family fast box for aid to the church in need came to £128. newtownards & comber parish non-stop draw week 27 27th october 2026 £100 no.194 pauline mccullough £50 no.215 betty ritchie £50 no. pearse stinson £50 collector’s prize-anne donaghy congratulations to all the winners! relics of the apostles & martyrs the parish of newtownards & comber has the privilege of being the custodian of relics of the holy apostles, martrys of the 2nd & 3rd centuries, in addition to other relics on temporary loan to the parish . the relics will be on display for the feast of all saints this weekend 31st october/1st november. those attending mass are invited to venerate the relics after mass. we ask for the prayers of the apostles and martyrs and all the saints. friendship club the club meets in st patrick’s parish centre, newtownards every wednesday 2pm-4pm. do come along to form and renew friendships. the club provides many opportunities for company, conversation and activities with many events organised throughout the year. please spread the word-invite friends along too!

communion antiphon mt 5:8-10 all: blessed are the clean of heart, for they shall see god. blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of god. blessed are they who are persecuted for the sake of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. purifying the chalice the celebrant says guietly: what has passed our lips as food, o lord, may we possess in purity of heart, that what has been given to us in time may be our healing for eternity. prayer after communion congregation kneels priest: let us pray. as we adore you, o god, who alone are holy and wonderful in all your saints, we implore your grace, so that, coming to perfect holiness in the fullness of your love, we may pass from this pilgrim table to the banquet of our heavenly homeland. through christ our lord. all: amen the concluding rites priest: the lord be with you. all: and with your spirit. priest: may god, the glory and joy of the saints, who has caused you to be strengthened by means of their outstanding prayers, bless you with unending blessings. all: amen priest: freed through their intercession from present ills and formed by the example of their holy way of life, may you be ever devoted to serving god and your neighbour. all: amen priest: so that, together with all, you may possess the joys of the homeland, where holy church rejoices that her children are admitted in perpetual peace to the company of the citizens of heaven. all: amen priest: and may the blessing of almighty god, the father, and the son, + and the holy spirit, come down on you and remain with you for ever. all: amen then the celebrant, with hands joined and facing the people, says: priest: goin peace. all: thanks be to god. imprimatur - gospel: matthew 22:34.40as we approach the month of november, the church invites us to remember in a special way those who gone before us in faith. praying for our deceased l oved ones is one of the beautiful traditions of our cath olic faith, reminding us that the bonds of love are not broken by death. as in previous years, i invite you to write the names of your deceased family members and friends o n the november dead lists and place them in the envelopes provided at the front of the church. throughout november, at every mass, we will remembe r all those whose names have been entrusted to our prayers. each envelope will be opened, the names read and placed upon the altar, a beautiful reminder that those we love are never forgotten, either by us or by god. on another note, it was a real joy to host a dioces an women's discernment evening here in st colmcille's on thursday evening. twenty young women gathered to reflect and pray about what god might be calling them to, particularly the possibility of religious life. it was wonderful to see such openness and generosity o f spirit. please keep these young women in your prayers as they continue to listen the lord's voice in their lives. in the gospel, jesus reminds us of the two great co mmandments: to love god with all our heart and to love our neighbour as ourselves. in many ways, both of these invitations are reflected in what we do as a parish. we show our love for god by being open to his call, and our love for one another through our prayers, o ur care and our remembrance of those who have gone before us. whether we are discerning what god wants of us, pra ying for someone we love, or simply offering a little kindness to another person, we ar living out those two great commandments. may november be a month of prayer, remembrance and renewed trust in god's love. st colmcilles
